baseline.reason: The same Docker reproducer triggered a sanitizer or race report only after introduction.; meta.json's root cause: Curl_ssl_scache_unlock(data) was moved to right after the critical section in Curl_ssl_scache_take(), before the trace-log statement that itself reads the shared peer->sessions list via Curl_llist_count() -- an unlocked read of lock-protected data. Source inspection confirms this: in post_intro, vtls_scache.c line 825 calls Curl_ssl_scache_unlock(data) and only afterwards (lines 828-833) calls Curl_llist_count(&peer->sessions) inside CURL_TRC_CF. In pre_intro, unlock happens at line 799 but the subsequent CURL_TRC_CF at line 801 reads only the already-taken local pointer *ps, not the shared list, so no unlocked shared-state access exists. In post_benign (the fix), Curl_ssl_scache_unlock(data) moves to line 837, after the CURL_TRC_CF/Curl_llist_count call, restoring lock coverage over the read. Using the same reproducer command (run_poc, no args, which invokes /poc/run.sh) on all three built versions: pre_intro exits 0 with 'done ok=1920 fail=0' and no sanitizer report; post_intro crashes (exit 66) with a genuine ThreadSanitizer data-race report whose write side is Curl_llist_insert_next <- Curl_llist_append <- cf_scache_peer_add_session <- Curl_ssl_scache_put (session insertion from another thread's TLS handshake) and whose (previously observed, same build/run) read side is Curl_llist_count <- Curl_ssl_scache_take at vtls_scache.c:828, i.e. the exact racy trace-log line -- this matches the original upstream TSan CI report in discussion.md (same function pair/race pattern: Curl_llist_insert_next racing Curl_llist_count in Curl_ssl_scache_take). post_benign again exits 0 with 'done ok=1920 fail=0' and no sanitizer report, matching pre_intro. The race is reproducible only in post_intro, is isolated to the exact introduced/fixed code, and is absent pre-intro and post-benign under the identical reproducer.
